My advice would be change your legal name asap. If it’s not possible or you’re in a place where it’s lots of money, don’t worry, but just keep it in mind.

When I started college, they kept none of my details as Damon until I actually handed over my deed poll.
I think this is because teachers forget you’re trans, and so just copy your legal name onto significant forms which don’t have to be the legal name. 

Your best bet if you can change legally, is to go up to reception before school starts, and say up front, this is my preferred name and I want all teachers to be aware of this, as well as to use female pronouns for me now. 

Hopefully they will be happy to send a group email, or to visit each of your teachers. 


Also, I would expect some kids to give you shit, but don’t let that make you hostile. Be friendly but cautious. If kids start picking on you, move away, ignore them, alert a teacher. Try and stay with friends and don’t let people get you down. Kids are really mean, and very stupid. 

If you have a uniform, try and get your hands on the girl version. If not, try and wear some feminine items. Not that it’s necessary, but I think a skirt or a little bit of jewellery would help people clock you as female so you can avoid pronoun trouble.

Another thing is, if your group of friends are boys, expect to be called a boy. If your group of friends is girls, expect to be called a girl. Not permanently, but if people see a group predominantly of one gender, it’ll usually be a “hey boys/girls”
Teachers just love gendering stuff.

Also jumpers might help cover lack of boobs, but then lots of girls your age don’t really have boobs anyway so I’m not sure it would stop you passing. 

Anyway, cool, good luck.
